To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the rutile phase of TiO2 intercalates lithium to a greater extent than the anatase phase and that the rutile TiO2 undergoes a structural phase change during the first lithium insertion.

the performance of a lithium polymer electrolytes cell using a titanium dioxide-based cathode is significantly better than the performance of the same cathode in a conventional lithium-ion cell, and that the performance is dependent on the polymorph of titanium dioxide used as cathode.
the anatase and rutle phases of titanium dioxide can be reversibly lithiated in a lithium polymer cell at 120°.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new electrode materials for lithium rechargeable batteries and in particular the use of titanium dioxide as an electrode for a lithium polymer electrolytes cell.
the use of titanium dioxide as an intercalation host for lithium ions in lithium polymer electrolyte cells.
the development of high energy density cathode materials based on titanium oxides for use in lithium polymer cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rutile phase is the only form of TiO2 to cycle with significant capacity at temperatures above ∼100°C.
rutile is the preferred form to be used as a positive electrode material for lithium polymer cells.
both anatase and rutule are capable of intercalation of Li ions, but the latter form is more suitable for use in a lithium polymer cell.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
both anatase and rutule are electrochemically active in the 0.5–2.0 V region.
both anatase and rutule can electrochemically intercalate lithium ions to a composition of LiTiO 2, but only the rutile form can be reversibly cycled at elevated temperatures.
rutile is a better electrode material for the cathode in a lithium polymer cell than anatase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of these materials is strongly dependent on temperature, and the rutile form of TiO2 can cycle with a significant capacity at temperatures above 100°C.
titanium dioxide can act as a cathode material for rechargeable lithium batteries operating at elevated temperatures.
the electrochemical insertion of lithium into the anatase phase is kinetically sluggish and the rutile phase is more stable and can be reversibly cycled at high rates.
